# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the open wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). It adds a magnetic ring that snaps the phone into alignment, and it charges at up to 15W. The magnetic design is based on Apple's MagSafe contributions ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey), [WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** (also sold as "Qi2 25W") is the newer version of that standard, launched in July 2025. It raises the cap to 25W, which the WPC says is nearly 70% more power. That is roughly 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The phone has to support it too. Among iPhones, that is the iPhone 16 and later, and Apple says the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro peak at 22.5W and the iPhone Air at 20W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)). The Pixel 10 Pro XL also supports it ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program for iPhones and accessories. It differs from Qi2 in a few ways:
- Apple-certified MagSafe chargers add an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify the charger, and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).
- Apple's current MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W, so in practice the two overlap on newer iPhones ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)).
- Chargers labeled only "MagSafe-compatible" usually aren't certified and often top out at 7.5W ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).

## Speeds by iPhone

| Charger | iPhone 12–15 and 17e | iPhone 16 and later (most models) |
|---|---|---|
| Qi2 (15W) | 15W | 15W |
| Qi2.2 / MagSafe 25W | 15W | Up to 20–25W |
| Non-certified "compatible" | ~7.5W | ~7.5W |

The 25W speed also needs a power adapter of about 30W or more. Most Android phones don't support Qi2 yet. Samsung's Galaxy lineup is only "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case.

## Which to buy
- **iPhone 16 or later:** a Qi2.2 / MagSafe 25W charger is worth it. [Apple's MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for it. The 2 m version is $49, and Macworld lists the 1 m version at about $39.
- **iPhone 15 or earlier:** a 15W Qi2 or MagSafe charger is enough, because 25W won't help.
- **Qi2.2 power bank:** The Verge's testing found the [Baseus PicoGo AM52](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w) the fastest of seven, reaching 65% on an iPhone 17 Pro Max in an hour. It's about $60. That link is a Dealectric affiliate link, which pays them a commission at no cost to you. The code AM52 was listed as saving $6.
